displayedInputs.question: What are the two properties of similar polygons? Select the correct option.

choices.A: Corresponding angles are equal, and corresponding sides are equal.
choices.B: Corresponding angles are equal, and corresponding sides are proportional.
choices.C: Corresponding sides are proportional, and the perimeters are equal.
choices.D: Corresponding angles are supplementary, and corresponding sides are proportional.

displayedInputs.question: Two similar polygons have a similarity ratio of \(2:3\). A side of the smaller polygon is 6 cm long. Find the length of the corresponding side of the larger polygon. (Unit: cm)
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.D: Any two polygons whose corresponding angles are equal are similar.

displayedInputs.question: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is similar to quadrilateral \(A'B'C'D'\) (vertices correspond in order). Given \(\angle A=80^\circ\), \(\angle B=95^\circ\), and \(\angle C=100^\circ\), find the degree measure of \(\angle D'\).

Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is similar to quadrilateral \(A'B'C'D'\) (vertices correspond in order). Given \(AB=4\), \(BC=6\), \(CD=8\), \(DA=10\), and \(A'B'=6\), find the perimeter of quadrilateral \(A'B'C'D'\).
In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=\angle D\) and \(\angle B=\angle E\). Are the triangles similar? Select the correct conclusion.

choices.C: They are similar because two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
choices.D: They are similar because all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional.

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A=50^\circ\) and \(\angle B=60^\circ\). In \(\triangle DEF\), \(\angle D=50^\circ\) and \(\angle F=70^\circ\). How are these two triangles related?

In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB=4\), \(AC=6\), and \(\angle A=50^\circ\). In \(\triangle DEF\), \(DE=6\), \(DF=9\), and \(\angle D=50^\circ\). Which criterion establishes that \(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF\)?

choices.A: Two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
choices.B: All three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional.
choices.C: Two pairs of corresponding sides are equal, and the included angles are equal.
choices.D: Two pairs of corresponding sides are proportional, and the included angles are equal.

displayedInputs.question: The side lengths of \(\triangle ABC\) are 2, 3, and 4. The shortest side of \(\triangle DEF\) is 4, and the corresponding side lengths of \(\triangle DEF\) and \(\triangle ABC\) are proportional. Find the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\).
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) is a point on \(AB\), \(\angle ACD=\angle B\), \(AD=4\), and \(AB=9\). Find the length of \(AC\).
The similarity ratio is \(2:3\). What is the area ratio? Select one.
Two similar triangles have a similarity ratio of \(3:5\). The smaller triangle has a perimeter of \(12\text{ cm}\). Find the perimeter of the larger triangle. (Unit: cm)
\(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF\), with a similarity ratio of \(2:3\). The area of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(24\text{ cm}^2\). Find the area of \(\triangle DEF\). (Unit: cm²)

\(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF\), and their areas are \(9\text{ cm}^2\) and \(25\text{ cm}^2\), respectively. The altitude to a side of \(\triangle ABC\) is \(6\text{ cm}\). Find the altitude to the corresponding side of \(\triangle DEF\). (Unit: cm)

\(\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEF\), and their areas are \(16\text{ cm}^2\) and \(36\text{ cm}^2\), respectively. The perimeters of the two triangles differ by \(10\text{ cm}\). Find the perimeter of the larger triangle, \(\triangle DEF\). (Unit: cm)
Segments \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(O\). Given \(AB\parallel CD\), \(OA=3\), \(OC=6\), and \(AB=4\), find the length of \(CD\).
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle ACB=90^\circ\), and \(CD\perp AB\) at \(D\). Given \(AD=4\) and \(BD=9\), find the length of \(CD\).

In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) lies on \(BC\), \(BD:DC=1:2\), and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\). Draw \(BE\) and extend it to intersect \(AC\) at \(F\). Find the value of \(AF/FC\). (Express the result as a fraction in lowest terms.)
A person who is \(1.6\text{ m}\) tall casts a shadow \(2\text{ m}\) long. At the same time, a flagpole casts a shadow \(15\text{ m}\) long. How tall is the flagpole? (Unit: m)
At the same time, a vertically placed bamboo pole \(2\text{ m}\) long casts a shadow \(1.5\text{ m}\) long, and a tree casts a shadow \(6\text{ m}\) long. Find the height of the tree. (Unit: m)

A plane mirror is placed on the ground. Xiaoming's eyes are \(1.5\text{ m}\) above the ground. Standing \(3\text{ m}\) from the mirror, he can just see the top of a tree in it. The distance from the mirror to the base of the tree is \(12\text{ m}\) (the person, mirror, and base of the tree lie on the same straight line). Find the height of the tree. (Unit: m)

The horizontal distance from the base of a flagpole to a wall is \(6\text{ m}\). The shadow of the top of the flagpole falls exactly on the wall, \(2\text{ m}\) above the ground. At the same time, a bamboo pole \(1\text{ m}\) long casts a shadow \(0.5\text{ m}\) long. Find the height of the flagpole. (Unit: m)
What is the area ratio of two figures with a homothety ratio of \(1:2\)? Select one.

Using the origin \(O\) as the center of homothety, enlarge point \(A(2,-3)\) by a factor of \(2\) (the corresponding point and \(A\) are on the same side of the center of homothety). Find the coordinates of the corresponding point \(A'\). Enter the horizontal coordinate first, followed by the vertical coordinate, separated by a comma.

Using the origin \(O\) as the center of homothety, enlarge point \(P(3,-1)\) by a factor of \(2\), with the corresponding point \(P'\) and \(P\) on opposite sides of the center of homothety. Find the coordinates of \(P'\). Enter the horizontal coordinate first, followed by the vertical coordinate, separated by a comma.
Which of the following statements about homothety is correct?

choices.C: Corresponding sides of homothetic figures are not necessarily parallel.
choices.D: The lines joining corresponding points of homothetic figures do not necessarily intersect at a single point.

displayedInputs.question: Using point \(P(1,1)\) as the center of homothety, enlarge point \(A(3,2)\) by a factor of \(3\). The corresponding point \(A'\) and \(A\) are on the same side of the center of homothety. Find the coordinates of \(A'\). Enter the horizontal coordinate first, followed by the vertical coordinate, separated by a comma.
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(BC=3\), and \(AB=5\). What is \(\sin A\)? (Express the result as a fraction in lowest terms.)
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(AC=4\), and \(BC=3\). Find \(\tan A\). (Express the result as a fraction in simplest form.)
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(AB=13\), and \(BC=5\). Which of the following statements is correct?
After every side of right triangle \(ABC\) is enlarged to 2 times its original length, how does the sine of acute angle \(A\) change?

choices.A: It becomes 2 times its original value.
choices.B: It becomes half its original value.

displayedInputs.question: In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(\tan A=3/4\), and the perimeter of triangle \(ABC\) is 36. Find the length of the hypotenuse \(AB\).
Find the values of \(\sin 30^\circ\), \(\cos 45^\circ\), and \(\tan 60^\circ\). Select the corresponding set in this order.
Calculate the value of \(\sin 30^\circ+\cos 60^\circ\).
Calculate the value of \(\tan 60^\circ\times\tan 30^\circ-(\cos 60^\circ)^2\). (Express the result as a fraction in simplest form.)
Given that \(A\) is an acute angle and \(2\cos A-\sqrt{3}=0\), find the measure of \(\angle A\) in degrees.
In triangle \(ABC\), \(|\sin A-1/2|+(\tan B-1)^2=0\), and both \(\angle A\) and \(\angle B\) are acute angles. Find the measure of \(\angle C\) in degrees.
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(\angle A=30^\circ\), and \(BC=4\). Find \(AC\) and \(AB\). Select the correct pair.
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(\angle A=30^\circ\), and \(AB=10\). Find the length of \(BC\).
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(BC=6\), and \(\tan A=3/4\). Find the lengths of \(AC\) and \(AB\). (Give your answers in this order, separated by a comma.)
